data.name: Chandrachur
data.gender_notes: Chandrachur is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Chandrachur is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Chandra' meaning moon and 'Chur' meaning power. This name is attributed to the Hindu deity Siva, who is often depicted holding a crescent moon on his forehead. Chandrachur represents the divine power and blessings of the moon god. The name Chandrachur carries the meaning “Moon God's Power” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chandrachur usually hope their child will grow to embody moon god's power and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Divine Blessings of the Moon God
data.etymology: Chandrachur belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Moon God's Power.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Chandrachur total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

The name is believed to channel the sacred power of Lord Shiva, promoting blessings, protection, and spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Chandrachur was a popular name for Hindu boys during the medieval period in Bengal. The name is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Chandra' meaning moon and 'Chur' meaning to devour, representing the power to absorb the moon's energy and light.

Chandrachur is also mentioned in ancient Indian texts such as the Mahabharata and the Puranas. In these texts, Chandrachur is the name of a Yadava prince who was a great warrior and a descendant of Krishna.
